title: Agent-to-Agent Finance: Blockchain Payments and Trust Infrastructure for Autonomous AI Agents
abstract: arXiv:2607.00245v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents are beginning to occupy a position between analytical tools and transacting counterparties. They can interpret goals, call external tools, negotiate with other agents, access data and computation, and in some settings initiate payments or blockchain transactions. This development creates a distinct problem for financial markets: if software agents can act economically under delegated authority, market participants need infrastructure for identity, authorisation, payment, verification, reputation and accountability. This chapter develops the concept of agent-to-agent finance as the layer of machine-mediated financial interaction in which autonomous agents discover counterparties, purchase services, express transaction intent, execute payments and generate auditable evidence. translated_title: 智能体间金融：面向自主AI智能体的区块链支付与信任基础设施
translated_abstract: 自主人工智能（AI）智能体正开始占据介于分析工具与交易对手方之间的位置。它们能够理解目标、调用外部工具、与其他智能体协商、访问数据与计算资源，并且在某些场景下能够发起支付或区块链交易。这一发展给金融市场带来了一个独特的问题：如果软件智能体能够在委托授权下进行经济活动，市场参与者就需要关于身份、授权、支付、验证、声誉和问责的基础设施。本章提出了“智能体间金融”（agent-to-agent finance）的概念，即由机器中介的金融交互层，在这一层中，自主智能体可以发现交易对手、购买服务、表达交易意图、执行支付并生成可审计的证据。本文的论点并非区块链是金融的通用底层，而是可编程结算、智能合约……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 本章提出了“智能体间金融”这一新概念，论证当自主AI智能体在委托授权下开展经济活动时，需要以区块链的可编程结算与智能合约为核心的信任基础设施来支撑身份、授权、支付、验证、声誉与问责机制。
en_tdlr: This chapter introduces the concept of agent-to-agent finance, arguing that autonomous AI agents acting economically under delegated authority require blockchain-based trust infrastructure—programmable settlement and smart contracts—to support identity, authorization, payment, verification, reputation, and accountability.
